title: Regional capacity handoff: probabilistic egress queueing & variant fallback safeguards
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose:
Design and implement a probabilistic region-to-region handoff policy plus model-variant demotion safeguards for cases where dedicated GPU capacity is exhausted. Goal is to reduce hard failovers to hosted endpoints, preserve per-tenant latency SLOs, and avoid systemic model-quality regressions when fallback variants are used.

Background:
We frequently see tenants hit dedicated pool limits during regional spikes. Current binary behavior (route-to-hosted immediately when dedicated full) causes sudden QoE shifts, potentially violating latency SLOs and surprising product owners. Prior tickets implemented several routing guardrails but left a gap: a tunable, observable intermediate layer that gradually shifts traffic and applies variant selection safety checks.

Requirements / Acceptance Criteria:
- New handoff mechanism must provide a tunable probability-based spill ratio per-tenant and per-region (0-100%) with hysteresis windows.
- When dedicated capacity is constrained, system should probabilistically send only a fraction of new requests to hosted endpoints while keeping most on dedicated, to smooth tail latency and model quality.
- Fallback to lower-cost or quantized model variants must be governed by a quality-safety gate: do not increase fallback rate above calibrated thresholds if eval metrics degrade.
- Route decisions must be traceable (route metadata attached to traces/logs) and surfaceable in Console (per-tenant policy, current spill ratio, recent metrics).
- Must include a rollback/circuit-breaker if hosted responses exceed latency or error thresholds for >N minutes.
- New configuration should be backwards compatible; default behavior for tenants without policy remains current hard-evacuation.

Design proposal (high-level):
1) Capacity Handoff Layer (CHL): lightweight policy service queried by request router. CHL exposes per-tenant region policies: soft_reserve, spill_probability, hysteresis_ms, min_dedicated_quota.
2) Probabilistic Egress: when dedicated reports shortfall for a tenant, router queries CHL which returns spill_probability p. Router samples a RNG per-request to decide egress: stay-on-dedicated with probability 1-p; spill to hosted with p. Sampling implemented in the router hot-path (no RPC) after periodic policy push for performance.
3) Graceful Backpressure Queue: a short per-tenant in-memory queue (<=200ms depth) that absorbs microbursts and reorders by priority (SLA tier), allowing short retries to land on newly freed dedicated slots.
4) Variant Safety Gate: fallback variants (quantized/cheaper) can be used only if recent quality window passes threshold. CHL maintains a rolling quality score per-variant per-tenant derived from eval prompts and synthetic probes. If quality drops >X% relative to baseline, demotion to that variant is blocked and traffic selection falls back to hosted full model or retries on dedicated.
5) Circuit Breakers & Rollback: telemetry monitors hosted latency and error rate. If hosted path latency P95 > threshold or error rate > threshold for >5 minutes, CHL forces p=0 for affected region/tenant until stabilized.

Config knobs (proposal):
- spill_probability: string (e.g. "0.25")
- hysteresis_ms: string ("60000")
- min_dedicated_quota: string ("5")
- egress_queue_ms: string ("200")
- variant_quality_threshold: string ("0.95")
- circuit_breaker_window_minutes: string ("5")

Trade-offs considered:
- Deterministic shifting (round-robin) vs probabilistic: probabilistic smooths short-timescale bursts and is simpler to reason about for fairness across requests. Deterministic bucketing creates tail effects for specific sessions.
- Router-side sampling vs centralized RPC: router-side sampling reduces latency but requires consistent policy propagation; mitigated by short push interval (5s) and fallback to RPC if policy missing.
- Queueing buys latency at expense of memory and complexity; capped very small to avoid amplification.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1: CHL proto + schema + push API; unit tests. (ENG)
- Week 2: Router integration (sampling and queue), end-to-end tests in staging. (ENG)
- Week 3: Variant safety gate integration (hooks to quality-service + config). (ENG + Applied ML)
- Week 4: Load test and chaos experiments, Console surface for policy and metrics. (ENG + Console)
- Week 5: Canary (1% tenants) -> expand to 20% -> roll to GA with runbook. (SRE + Solutions)

Testing plan:
- Synthetic spike tests with per-tenant burst patterns to validate spill ratios approximate configured p within statistical bounds.
- Chaos: kill dedicated backends mid-spike to measure platform recovery and circuit-breaker behavior.
- Quality safety gating verified by injecting degraded responses on quantized variant and ensuring gate prevents demotion.
- A/B compared to current hard-evacuation for cost/latency/QoE metrics.

Metrics to track (per-tenant, per-region):
- Dedicated utilization, hosted egress rate, observed spill_probability (empirical), tail latency (P50/P95/P99), error rate, quality-score delta for variant, time-in-circuit-breaker.

Console & Observability changes needed:
- New per-tenant view: configured spill_probability, current effective p, recent quality score, circuit-breaker state.
- Tracing: router decision span must include policy_version and sampled outcome.

Runbook (short):
- If hosted P95 > configured threshold: CHL auto-zeroes p for impacted region -> notify on-call and SRE investigates hosted fleet.
- If variant quality score drops below threshold: mark variant quarantined, route customers to dedicated or hosted full model until probe passes.
- Manual override: SRE/PM can set per-tenant p via Console to 0/1 for emergency.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to price probabilistic hosted usage for tenants on committed dedicated contracts? (billing team sync required).
- Long-lived sessions: should we sticky route subsequent tokens of a chat to the same egress outcome to avoid consistency issues? (Performance vs consistency tradeoff).
- Backpressure semantics when hosted latency is high: should we increase p to reduce dedicated pressure or pause spill entirely?

Acceptance criteria checklist (pre-merge):
- [ ] CHL API endpoints + schema implemented and unit-tested.
- [ ] Router-side sampling integrated and covered by integration tests.
- [ ] Variant safety gate hooked to quality metrics and prevents unsafe demotion.
- [ ] Console shows per-tenant policy and recent metrics.
- [ ] Runbook written and SRE rehearsed canary rollback.
